dataset: Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer (569 rows, 30 numeric features)
split: Stratified 80:20 train/test; training split into 70:30 fit/adaptation; adaptation split 50:50 monitoring/update. Monitoring data select policy; update data fit recalibration/retraining; test remains untouched.

selector_rule.retrain: delta ROC-AUC <= -0.03 OR delta malignant recall <= -0.10 OR delta Brier >= 0.05
selector_rule.recalibrate: if not retrain and delta Brier >= 0.02 OR abs(calibration intercept) >= 0.50 OR calibration slope < 0.80 OR > 1.20

reference: Same monitoring observations before synthetic shift; observed metrics are computed after shift. This is a controlled paired diagnostic, not a deployable unsupervised detector.
comparison: Adaptive selector vs fixed no-update, fixed recalibration, fixed retraining. All use identical fit/update/test partitions.
bootstrap: 2,000 paired bootstrap resamples of 10 seed-level differences; intervals reflect split/seed variability only.
limitations: Only 10 seeds and two model families (Logistic Regression and Random Forest).
Synthetic shifts on a small benchmark dataset; not external clinical validation.
The selector uses labelled monitoring outcomes and a paired unshifted reference; it is not an unsupervised real-world drift detector.
The small monitoring and update partitions make calibration estimates noisy.
The thresholds are prespecified heuristic thresholds, not clinically validated or optimized.
Balanced prevalence condition uses balanced resampling, not a prospective prior-shift design.
Repeated random splits overlap in source observations; bootstrap intervals are not population-level confidence intervals.
